what: The two SuperCollider definitions /grains/ loads into the browser engine. Compiled by sclang ON THE BOARD, not built here.
why: /grains/ claims the same graph runs in the browser and on the Raspberry Pi. That is only true if these bytes came out of the same Engine_Pappus.sc the board's service compiles, so they are a build artefact OF THE BOARD and are produced there.
howToRemake: scp rig/box/norns/{Engine_Pappus.sc,PosSource.sc,writedefs.scd} to the board, put the classes where sclang reads them (/home/positron/.local/share/SuperCollider/Extensions/pappus/lib/), then: XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/tmp/rt QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen PAPPUS_TINY=1 PAPPUS_OUT=/tmp/defs sclang -u 57125 /tmp/writedefs.scd — then copy the files here and re-run this file's hashes.
compiledOn: raspberrypi, the studio board, sclang 3.13.0, 2026-09-13, PAPPUS_TINY=1

pappus-tiny.scsyndef.note: byte-identical to the capture in research/supercollider-browser-2026-09.md §10, taken by a different script on a different run

possource.scsyndef.note: one Osc.ar per voice reading a wavetable — plan-twins §4a-i weighed the explicit-SinOsc rendering at 1,151 UGens and 46,815 bytes, which scsynth refused

guard: workers/view/build.mjs REFUSES the build when any hash above disagrees with the file on disk. A stale artefact is otherwise silent in the worst direction: the browser would run an OLD graph while the board runs a new one, and the page's whole claim is that they are the same.
